newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed rejects Russia coup accusations.
newsitem.headline: Lebed rejects Russia coup accusations.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed on Wednesday rejected accusations by Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov that he was preparing to seize power.
"There cannot even be talk of an attempted coup d'etat," he told a crowd of reporters outside his office in central Moscow.
"Let's all sleep quietly. I guarantee that nothing will happen," said Lebed, who has made a number of powerful enemies since being given the job of Security Council secretary in late June.

Kulikov, his chief political opponent, said earlier on Wednesday that Lebed was planning to take power by force. The two men are locked in a power struggle which has worsened since President Boris Yeltsin announced on September 5 he planned to have heart surgery.
"I won't resign. I am not sure that I'll be the one to be fired. It will be Kulikov who is fired," said Lebed, who in August told Yeltsin he would have to choose between one of the two men.
But the Russian leader ignored the ultimatum, telling Lebed to go back to work and stop complaining.
